topic: Complete SI-PAG orientation under selection and unknown-target interventions. On finite causally sufficient DAGs in Dai et al.'s full published pre-treatment-selection interventional-twin-graph compatibility class, with observational and unknown-target soft-intervention regimes supplied as oracle regime MAGs, define the canonical SI-PAG by endpoint-mark invariance over the entire class. Give a finite sound within- and cross-regime orientation calculus whose monotone mark closure terminates after polynomially many endpoint updates, prove mark completeness by showing closure equals the canonical SI-PAG and every residual circle has two compatible orientation witnesses, and derive a complete population CDIS algorithm on the same class. Do not claim polynomial conditional-independence discovery. Use Dai et al.'s two-variable equivalence witness and sciPlex2/A549 workflow, and distinguish Jaber's no-selection theory and Luo et al.'s post-treatment-selection F-PAG.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a canonical SI-PAG and a finite sound and mark-complete within- and cross-regime orientation calculus for Dai et al.'s full causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection class with unknown-target soft interventions.

source_refs.claim: The published theorem proves CDIS soundness with oracle CI tests, but supplies neither a canonical class representative nor a mark-completeness theorem.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Zhang gives complete endpoint-orientation rules for one observational MAG equivalence class with latent confounding and selection, not for regime MAGs coupled by an interventional twin graph.
source_refs.author: Jiji Zhang

source_refs.claim: Jaber et al. prove sample-limit mark completeness for unknown-target soft interventions in non-Markovian systems without Dai's pre-treatment-selection twin-world semantics.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Murat Kocaoglu, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.excerpt: MPDAG total-effect invariance witness: an orientation-cut certificate over DAG completions.
if the source-cover recursion fails, then there exist two finite binary semi-Markovian SCMs

open_problems.why_unsolved: Dai et al. characterize compatibility through regime-specific twin MAGs and prove only that CDIS orientations are sound; ordinary FCI completeness does not show that all marks invariant under the joint twin-graph restrictions are derivable, while Jaber et al.'s complete unknown-target calculus lacks the basal selection world. The prior MPDAG and data-fusion proposals contribute only donor architectures—semantic invariance over completions and paired nonidentification witnesses—not the required coupled state space. The first missing proof step is a realizability-preserving extension lemma for a partially oriented family of regime MAGs: every residual circle must extend to two globally compatible twin-graph witnesses without breaking acyclicity, ancestral/maximal structure, pre-treatment selection, or cross-regime intervention constraints.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite monotone endpoint-rule system whose least closure equals endpoint-mark invariance over the full compatible class, with two compatible witnesses for every residual circle and a complete population-oracle CDIS algorithm using only polynomially many strict mark updates, not a polynomial CI-discovery claim.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its move from real pre-selection examples to augmented-graph failure, twin-graph semantics, and the remaining gap between sound discovery and a represented equivalence class.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interventions are applied after selective enrollment -> ordinary augmented graphs misread cross-regime invariances -> interventional twin graphs give the correct compatibility class -> a canonical SI-PAG and complete orientation calculus must represent exactly that class

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the invariant-mark proof using discriminating paths and orientation-extension witnesses from a single MAG class to a jointly constrained family of regime MAGs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both conclusions equate syntactic endpoint closure with semantic invariance, but the SI-PAG witnesses must preserve cross-regime twin-graph compatibility.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the Ψ-Markov augmented-I-MAG representation and its sound-and-complete cross-distribution orientation argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already resolves unknown-target soft-intervention mark completeness, isolating pre-treatment basal-world selection as the additional proof constraint.

method_exemplars.technique: After population completeness, port the sparse FCI consistency proof by conditioning on simultaneous correctness of all queried CI and invariance tests before deterministic closure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest estimation rung for exact recovery of a PAG-like invariant-mark object under selection.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend Dai et al.'s pre-treatment-selection and unknown-target soft-intervention equivalence theory from causally sufficient DAGs to systems with latent common causes.

source_refs.claim: The published CDIS theory assumes causal sufficiency and faithfulness, leaving latent common causes outside its model class.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Jaber et al. handle latent-confounded unknown-target soft interventions and prove completeness, but have no pre-treatment-selection twin world.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Murat Kocaoglu, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Luo et al. combine latent confounding with post-treatment selection in complete F-PAG/F-FCI theory, a different timing model from Dai's pre-treatment selection.
source_refs.author: Gongxu Luo, Loka Li, Guangyi Chen, Haoyue Dai, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The adjacent theories occupy different corners: Jaber et al. allow latent confounding without pre-selection, Dai et al. model pre-selection under causal sufficiency, and Luo et al. allow latent confounding under post-treatment selection. Adding latent common causes to Dai's twin model creates bidirected inducing paths and ordered-collider constraints, so the published reduction to adjacencies and v-structures can fail. The first proof step that changes is the equivalence criterion itself: general MAG discriminating paths must be reconciled simultaneously across basal and reality worlds and across unknown intervention targets.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient equivalence criterion for latent-confounded pre-treatment interventional twin graphs, a canonical invariant-mark representative, and a sound-and-complete oracle recovery algorithm with explicit opposing compatible witnesses for every noninvariant mark.

writing_exemplar.why: Retain its pre-selection motivation and twin-world formulation while making hidden common causes the precise scope boundary being crossed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pre-selection invalidates standard interventional graphs -> twin graphs repair the causally sufficient case -> real systems also contain hidden common causes -> characterize the latent-confounded pre-selection equivalence class

method_exemplars.technique: Replace adjacency-plus-v-structure equivalence by colliders with order and discriminating-path equivalence for general maximal ancestral graphs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Latent confounding introduces exactly the MAG-equivalence phenomena absent from Dai's causally sufficient reduction.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift unknown-target soft-intervention invariances into augmented I-MAGs and adapt the Ψ-FCI completeness construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the latent-confounded intervention half of the desired theory, with basal-world selection as the new coupling.

method_exemplars.technique: Port uniform CI-error control and deterministic FCI correctness to the latent SI-PAG sample analogue.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The new canonical representative would be a PAG-like causal structure with a direct exact-recovery inference rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize which selected-population or target-population causal effects are uniformly identifiable from observational and unknown-target soft-intervention laws over a Dai-style pre-treatment-selection twin-graph equivalence class.

source_refs.claim: Dai et al. establish structural discovery and soundness but do not give a complete causal-effect identification theory over the resulting twin-graph classes.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim give a complete algorithm and graphical failure criterion for causal-effect identification from an ordinary PAG.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Jiji Zhang, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Bareinboim, Tian, and Pearl characterize recoverability from selection-biased observational data when the selection diagram is specified.
source_refs.author: Elias Bareinboim, Jin Tian, Judea Pearl

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary PAG identification quantifies over one observational MAG class, while selection recoverability starts from a specified selection diagram. A Dai compatibility class instead varies the causal DAG, selection mechanism, and unknown intervention targets while coupling observed reality to an unobserved basal world. Neither adjacent algorithm decides whether one functional is shared by every compatible twin model. The missing step is a complete reduction from the coupled class to either a common functional of the selected regime laws or a pair of compatible twin models agreeing on all supplied laws but disagreeing on the query.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete graphical algorithm that returns an identifying functional of the available selected observational and interventional laws for a specified causal effect, or a regime-explicit pair of compatible twin models proving nonidentifiability.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its twin-world setup as the structural substrate, then pivot from learning the class to causal queries stable across the class.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pre-selected interventions require twin-world semantics -> available laws determine only a compatibility class -> scientific use requires causal effects stable over that class -> characterize exactly when those effects are computable

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the complete PAG-ID recursion and its graphical failure certificate to a class coupled across selected intervention regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require one identifying expression to remain valid uniformly over an equivalence class rather than a fully specified graph.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt selection-recoverability reductions and compatible-model counterexamples for failed recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target functional must be recovered from distributions conditioned by selection, now supplemented and constrained by twin-regime information.

method_exemplars.technique: For an identified selected-to-target mean, adapt outcome-regression, sampling-weight, and doubly robust estimators together with their asymptotic analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a concrete estimator and inference rung for causal means transported from a selectively enrolled sample to a target population.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize and completely recover causal structure when one unknown-target intervention study contains both pre-treatment enrollment selection and post-treatment measurement or quality-control selection.

source_refs.claim: Dai et al. model selection before intervention in a basal world; their framework does not provide a complete joint theory with a second selection event after treatment.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Luo et al. give complete F-PAG/F-FCI theory for post-treatment selection and latent confounding, a different causal timing and graph representation from Dai's pre-treatment model.
source_refs.author: Gongxu Luo, Loka Li, Guangyi Chen, Haoyue Dai, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two timing regimes have complete or partial theories separately but no shared Markov representation in the located literature. Dai's basal-world selection can preserve a marginal while changing a conditional after intervention, whereas Luo's reality-world filtering can produce a different invariance signature and is encoded by F-PAG rather than an interventional twin graph. The first proof step that changes is the graph itself: a joint model needs separate pre- and post-selection nodes and a derivation of the conditional independences surviving conditioning on both before either equivalence or orientation proof can be reused.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint pre/post-selection intervention graph with a necessary-and-sufficient equivalence criterion, a canonical invariant-mark representative, and a sound-and-complete population orientation algorithm that separates causal edges from both selection timings.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its selection-timing contrast and biological quality-control motivation while making simultaneous enrollment and post-treatment filtering the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Selection timing changes cross-regime invariances -> CDIS and F-FCI solve different timings -> real studies can enroll selectively and later filter samples -> a joint equivalence theory must distinguish both mechanisms from causation

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the basal-world interventional twin-graph construction and its regime-MAG compatibility argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It correctly represents the pre-treatment half and identifies where a reality-world selection node must be added.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over F-PAG edge semantics and F-FCI rules that distinguish post-treatment selection-induced paths from direct causal links.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the post-treatment half and a complete orientation proof whose cases can seed the joint calculus.

method_exemplars.technique: After population identification, adapt the uniform-test-error consistency proof for a sample joint-PAG recovery procedure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A canonical joint representative would admit exact graph recovery as a direct estimation rung under sparse high-dimensional conditions.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine sparsity, signal-strength, and regime-sample-size conditions under which estimated within-regime conditional independences and cross-regime conditional invariances consistently recover the canonical pre-treatment-selection SI-PAG.

source_refs.claim: Dai et al.'s formal CDIS guarantee uses oracle CI tests; simulation and sciPlex2/A549 analysis do not constitute an exact graph-recovery limit theorem.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Ignavier Ng, Jianle Sun, Zeyu Tang, Gongxu Luo, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Colombo et al. prove sparse high-dimensional consistency for observational FCI and RFCI with latent and selection variables, but not coupled multi-regime invariance testing.
source_refs.author: Diego Colombo, Marloes H. Maathuis, Markus Kalisch, Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: Chakraborty and Shojaie prove high-dimensional consistency of nonparametric FCI-stable using conditional distance covariance tests.
source_refs.author: Shubhadeep Chakraborty, Ali Shojaie

source_refs.claim: The sci-Plex study supplies compound-dose perturbation regimes in A549 and other cell lines, grounding unequal regime sizes and post-sequencing filtering as practical issues.
source_refs.author: Sanjay R. Srivatsan, José L. McFaline-Figueroa, Vijay Ramani, et al.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing FCI consistency proofs control a single observational CI-search process. CDIS additionally pools observational and intervention regimes, encodes conditional distribution invariance through intervention indicators, prunes from cross-regime implications, and propagates orientations between regime PAGs. The usual single-graph uniform test-error event therefore does not suffice: one must control an adaptive family of within- and cross-regime tests with unequal sample sizes and prove that deterministic monotone closure cannot amplify a local test error into a false invariant mark. This is a statistical recovery question, not a polynomial CI-discovery claim.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A specified sample CDIS procedure and a finite-sample exact-recovery bound or asymptotic consistency theorem for the canonical SI-PAG under explicit sparsity, strong-faithfulness or beta-min, smoothness, and per-regime sample-size conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its population-to-sciPlex2/A549 transition to motivate why oracle completeness needs a separate finite-sample recovery theorem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Twin-graph invariances orient more marks in population -> CDIS assumes exact oracle answers -> sciPlex2 has finite and unequal perturbation regimes with filtering -> derive conditions under which estimated tests recover the same SI-PAG

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the sparse FCI proof based on simultaneous correctness of all queried partial-correlation tests and deterministic correctness conditional on that event.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the closest graph-level exact-recovery template in the presence of selection variables.

method_exemplars.technique: Use conditional distance covariance and its uniform high-dimensional error analysis for nonlinear and non-Gaussian CI queries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sciPlex setting is nonlinear, and CDIS writes regime invariance as conditional-independence queries involving intervention indicators.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the kernel conditional-independence statistic and its null approximation for pooled-regime tests involving an intervention indicator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Cross-regime conditional invariance in CDIS has exactly the conditional-independence form handled by KCI.

literature_map:
Dai et al. (ICLR 2025, arXiv:2503.07302) introduce interventional twin graphs for pre-treatment selection, unknown-target soft interventions, and causal sufficiency.
Their equivalence theorem compares regime-specific twin MAGs; the special twin structure reduces its criterion to adjacencies and v-structures.
Their two-variable example makes a selected no-edge model observationally/interventionally equivalent to an unselected directed-edge model, fixing a genuine nonidentifiability boundary.
CDIS runs observational FCI, constructs intervention-regime PAGs, and propagates cross-regime refinements; Theorem 3 proves soundness with oracle CI tests, not mark completeness.
Zhang (Artificial Intelligence 2008, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2008.08.001) proves complete ordinary FCI endpoint rules with latent confounding and selection.
Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes (Annals of Statistics 2009, arXiv:0908.3605) characterize MAG equivalence through ordered colliders and discriminating paths.
Jaber et al. (NeurIPS 2020) give a complete Ψ-Markov procedure for unknown-target soft interventions without Dai's pre-treatment-selection twin semantics.
Andrews, Spirtes, and Cooper (AISTATS 2020), Wang, Qin, and Zhou (Artificial Intelligence 2023), and Venkateswaran and Perković (arXiv:2407.07338) study completeness under narrower background-knowledge restrictions.
Those background-knowledge results do not establish realizability of arbitrary endpoint choices under Dai's coupled cross-regime twin constraints.
Luo et al. (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2509.25800) develop complete F-PAG/F-FCI theory for post-treatment selection with latent confounding.
Luo's post-treatment selection changes the graph semantics and invariance signature, so F-PAG cannot substitute for the requested pre-treatment SI-PAG.
Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (ICML 2019, arXiv:1812.06209) give complete causal-effect identification over ordinary PAGs, not twin-graph compatibility classes.
Bareinboim, Tian, and Pearl (AAAI 2014) treat recovery from selection-biased data when a selection diagram is specified, leaving the varying-selection-mechanism twin class untouched.
Colombo et al. (Annals of Statistics 2012, arXiv:1104.5617) and Chakraborty–Shojaie (Entropy 2022, arXiv:2106.11415) provide FCI consistency templates, not CDIS's coupled regime tests.
Srivatsan et al. (Science 2020, doi:10.1126/science.aax6234) provide the sci-Plex A549 perturbation workflow used by Dai and ground finite, unequal intervention regimes and filtering concerns.
